One measure goes by two names. The headline and lede call the gate 'balanced-accuracy', while the gate matrix, scatter, Watch and appendix call it 'Overall accuracy' (e.g. 'Overall accuracy: 90.7% against 90%'). The page also reports a separate traffic-weighted accuracy (92.2% for Brisk-S few-shot), which a reader would naturally take 'overall accuracy' to mean. Read that way, Atlas-M zero-shot (91.2%) would pass the gate the matrix says it fails. The claim and the lede rank Brisk-S few-shot against Nano-XS few-shot on cost ($40.00 against $1.90 per million turns; 'saving $1,143 a month') without saying who served each model. These qualifiers sit only in the caption and Method. Fix: in the claim sentence and the lede, say these are costs as this run's unnamed provider routing served them, and that the monthly gap assumes the volume is in turns.

Fix: say the High applies to the balanced-accuracy and cell-floor readings, and that the latency gate stays open until the production p95 measurement with an interval. - Latency: p95 per configuration on the test setup, with no interval stated.
- Cost: Cost per million turns as this run was served; the served model is named for each arm, the provider for none. Monthly figures read the declared volume of 30,000,000 as turns, which the input does not state.
